question.problem:
Let $X$ and $Y$ be discrete random variables with the joint probability mass function $f(x,y)$ shown below.

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.35$ | $0.25$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.25$ | $0.15$ |

If $F(x,y)$ is the joint CDF of $X$ and $Y,$ find $F(2,0).$
question.worked_solution:
If $X$ and $Y$ are discrete random variables with the joint probability mass function $f(x,y),$ then the corresponding joint CDF is given by

$$
F(x,y)=P(X\le x,Y\le y)={\sum }_{{x}_{i}\le x}{\sum }_{{y}_{i}\le y}f({x}_{i},{y}_{i}).
$$

By definition, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}F(2,0) & =P(X\le 2,Y\le 0).\end{aligned}
$$

We start by highlighting all cells in the table that correspond to $X\le 2,Y\le 0.$

| $f$ | $Y=0$ | $Y=1$ |
| --- | --- | --- |
| $X=1$ | $0.35$ | $0.25$ |
| $X=2$ | $0.25$ | $0.15$ |

Therefore, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}F(2,0) & ={\sum }_{x\le 2}{\sum }_{y\le 0}f(x,y) \\  & =f(1,0)+f(2,0) \\  & =0.35+0.25 \\  & =0.6.\end{aligned}
$$
